story.fullStory:
Lobo's "I'd Love You To Want Me" reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100. "I'd Love You to Want Me" is a song by American singer-songwriter Lobo.

It was released in September 1972 as the second single from his second album Of a Simple Man.

The song was Lobo's highest-charting hit on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, where it spent two weeks at No.

The song peaked at #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 14 weeks on the chart.

It became a gold record.

When released in the United Kingdom in 1972, the song failed to reach the UK Singles Chart; however, a re-release of the single in 1974, on the UK record label, peaked at No.

In 1964, while attending the University of South Florida, LaVoie joined a band called the Sugar Beats and met producer Phil Gernhard.

He recorded a regional hit for the band, a cover of Johnny Rivers' song "What Am I Doing Here?" During the 1960s, LaVoie performed with many other bands, including US Male, The Uglies, and Me and the Other Guys.
